Article Title: Highest-ever! Afghanistan make historic leap, overtake Sri Lanka, England and West Indies in ODI rankings
Article Text:
Afghanistan cricket team (Pic credit: ICC)

From debutants to a force in world cricket

Winning momentum fuels historic rankings rise

Afghanistan have reached a historic milestone in international cricket, breaking into the top six of the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings for the first time and moving ahead of former world champions Sri Lanka, England and the West Indies.The Afghans have climbed to sixth place in the latest rankings, surpassing Sri Lanka to secure their highest-ever position in the 50-over format. It marks another significant chapter in the remarkable rise of a side that made its ODI debut only in 2009 and has steadily established itself among the most competitive teams in international cricket.Their latest achievement is particularly significant given the established cricketing nations they have overtaken. Afghanistan had already moved ahead of Bangladesh, England and the West Indies in the rankings and have now gone past Sri Lanka to break into the top six.Afghanistan's rise has been built on consistent performances and landmark victories against some of the biggest names in the game.Since making their ODI debut in 2009, they have won 96 of their 191 matches, boasting an impressive win-loss ratio of 1.09. Their progress gathered momentum during the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, where they produced memorable victories over former champions Pakistan and Sri Lanka.They carried that confidence into the shortest format, reaching the semi-finals of the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup for the first time. The campaign further underlined their growing stature, as they demonstrated their ability to compete with the world's leading sides on the biggest stage.Afghanistan's latest climb has been backed by an impressive run of results in recent months.They began their recent surge with a dominant 4-0 away series victory over Ireland before maintaining an unbeaten record in the tri-series involving Zimbabwe and Bangladesh.Their impressive form has also extended to T20Is. Afghanistan recently completed a 3-0 series whitewash against Zimbabwe, sealing the clean sweep with a convincing seven-wicket victory in the third and final match in Sharjah on Sunday.The Afghans will now turn their attention to the longest format, with a two-match Test series against Zimbabwe next on the schedule.
Article Summary: Afghanistan have broken into the top six of the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings for the first time. The Afghans have climbed to sixth place in the latest rankings, surpassing Sri Lanka to secure their highest-ever position. It marks another significant chapter in the remarkable rise of a side that made its ODI debut only in 2009.

Article Title: Leander Paes to run for AITA vice-prez
Article Text:
Leander Paes (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: In a move filled with surprise and intrigue, Leander Paes has decided to run for the lone vice-president's post in the All India Tennis Association (AITA) elections, scheduled for Nov. 27.The 18-time Grand Slam winner's candidature was revealed by Chintan Parikh, AITA's interim president, in a press release on Sunday."Parikh will contest for president and Paes for vice-president. Both of them will be supported by a capable team comprising an honorary secretary, treasurer, two joint secretaries and other executive committee members. These names will be decided in the next few days," the press release said.Parikh said his partnership with Paes, who is the president of the Bengal Tennis Association, was finalised after a meeting between the two in Kolkata on Friday.As per the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, a candidate must have completed at least one term as an office-bearer in a state association or on the executive committee of the national body to be eligible to run for president. Paes was elected to the BTA's top job last November.Despite being the only Olympic medallist on the Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM) roster, he chose not to contest the AITA presidency. Grand Slam winners Mahesh Bhupathi and Sania Mirza, however, have filed their nominations..
Article Summary: Leander Paes will run for the lone vice-president's post in the All India Tennis Association (AITA) elections. The 18-time Grand Slam winner's candidature was revealed by Chintan Parikh, AITA's interim president, in a press release on Sunday.

Article Title: East Bengal women off to winning start at AFC Women's Champions League

Article Title: Lessons from Prakash fuel Tirthank Pegu’s Youth Olympics push
Article Text:
Tirthank Pegu

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: As Tirthank Pegu prepares for the biggest competition of his young career, his biggest takeaway from the last few months has little to do with lap times or race strategies.The Assam swimmer, who will represent India in the 100m and 200m butterfly at Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, spent six weeks training in Europe, including a stint alongside India’s most accomplished butterfly swimmer, Sajan Prakash. While the sessions in Spain and Scotland helped sharpen his technique, Pegu says the lessons he learnt outside the pool could prove just as valuable.“My target was to go sub-two minutes in the 200m butterfly because Sajan Prakash is the only Indian swimmer who has achieved that. Training with him taught me a lot, not only about the event itself but also about life beyond swimming,” Pegu told STOI.Fresh from a personal-best performance at Singapore National Age Group Swimming Championships in March, where he clocked 2:00.96 in the 200m butterfly to grab bronze after improving from his previous best of 2:02.56, Pegu travelled to Spain for a three-week high-altitude camp before heading directly to Scotland for another three weeks of preparation.The Singapore meet, however, proved to be a turning point.“It gave me a huge mental boost. Dropping two seconds in an event like the 200m butterfly made me more confident in myself and in my coach’s training,” said the 18-year-old.That confidence only grew during his European camps, where he had the opportunity to observe first-hand how elite swimmers approach their craft.According to Pegu, one of the most important lessons from Prakash was understanding that success in swimming is built away from the pool as much as inside it.“He taught me that swimming is not only about training in the water. It’s about your lifestyle, the habits you maintain and the discipline you follow every day. The way you live your life shows up in the pool,” said Pegu during a virtual interaction from Dakar on Saturday.The youngster believes those conversations helped strengthen him mentally as he chases one of the biggest goals of his career. While qualifying for the Youth Olympics fulfilled a dream he shared with his father, Pegu has also developed a larger purpose.“When I was training in Delhi, there were times when I felt negative. A lot of people still don’t believe that Indian swimmers can achieve great results at major international events like the Asian Games or the Commonwealth Games,” said Pegu, who currently trains at Inspire Institute of Sport in Vijayanagar, Karnataka.The 18-year-old hopes strong performances by Indian swimmers on the global stage can change those perceptions. “My goal is to help Indian swimming reach a level where people take us seriously and support us more,” he added.For now, however, his complete focus remains on the Youth Olympics, and the 100m and 200m butterfly events he will compete in.Armed with confidence from a breakthrough year, six weeks of training in Europe and lessons learned from veteran Prakash, Pegu hopes to turn those experiences into a medal-winning performance on the biggest stage of his junior career.
Article Summary: Tirthank Pegu will represent India in the 100m and 200m butterfly at Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal. The 18-year-old spent six weeks training in Europe, including a stint alongside India’s most accomplished butterfly swimmer, Sajan Prakash.

Article Title: No Starc, Cummins or Hazlewood in squad as Australia name several new faces for England series
Article Text:

Australia have named several new faces in their white-ball squads for the upcoming series against England, with young fast bowler Mahli Beardman and allrounders Jack Edwards and Liam Scott among those receiving call-ups.Batting prospects Ollie Peake and Jake Fraser-McGurk have also been included, along with wicketkeepers Lachlan Shaw and Sam Harper. Mitchell Marsh will captain both the ODI and T20I teams."These ODI and T20 matches provide several players, many of whom have had opportunities on recent tours, with a great chance to further demonstrate their ability against very strong opposition," said chairman of selectors George Bailey.Beardman, Peake, Edwards, Scott, Nikhil Chaudhary and Joel Davies have made their white-ball debuts in recent times. Shaw and Harper are the only uncapped players in the squads."They are good examples of players who have had an opportunity at the international level and have continued working on their game from what they learnt from those experiences," added Bailey.Australia will play three ODIs against England at home from November 13 to 18, followed by a five-match T20I series.The matches will give the next generation of Australian players an opportunity to make a case for selection ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.With a home Test series against New Zealand coming up, fast bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have been rested from the white-ball squads. The trio featured in Australia's 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.Travis Head, Alex Carey, Matt Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and Cameron Green have been named in the ODI squad but will not feature in the T20Is.After the New Zealand series, Australia will travel to India for a five-Test series. That will be followed by a 150th anniversary Test against England in Melbourne and an Ashes campaign."We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule," said Bailey, referring to Australia's Test players."To manage this workload, each player's build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focussed on individual's physical and mental preparation."
Article Summary: Australia have named several new faces in their white-ball squads for the upcoming series against England. Young fast bowler Mahli Beardman and allrounders Jack Edwards and Liam Scott among those receiving call-ups. Batting prospects Ollie Peake and Jake Fraser-McGurk have also been included.

Article Title: Asian Champions Trophy Hockey: India look to continue winning run against China
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Mandeep makes a strong statement

Fulton wants India to improve after the break

China present a different challenge

Other Asian Champions Trophy matches on Thursday

Match Start time Malaysia vs South Korea 2.30 pm Japan vs Bangladesh 4.45 pm India vs China 7 pm

India squad

India will look to build on their strong start to the Asian Champions Trophy when they face China in their second round-robin match on Thursday. The five-time champions began their title defence with a big win over Bangladesh and will be keen to maintain their momentum against a young Chinese side.India, who recently won their second successive Asian Games gold medal to secure direct qualification for the Los Angeles Olympics, dominated Bangladesh in their opening match. Bangladesh replaced Pakistan in the tournament after the latter refused to travel to India, citing security reasons.The match was largely played in Bangladesh's half, with India controlling the contest. While Bangladesh were not expected to pose a major challenge, India's ability to score from both field play and penalty corners was an encouraging sign.The Harmanpreet Singh-led side scored eight field goals and five goals from set pieces against Bangladesh on Tuesday.Veteran forward Mandeep Singh was among the standout performers, scoring a hat-trick. His return to form comes at an important time, with national selectors expected to assess the players after the tournament.Mandeep was reportedly among four senior players who could be phased out after the ACT.The other three were Jarmanpreet Singh, Amit Rohidas and Nilakanta Sharma.Nilakanta announced on Tuesday that the tournament would be his last at the international level. However, Mandeep and Jarmanpreet are keen to continue playing.Apart from Mandeep's three goals, captain Harmanpreet, Dilpreet Singh and vice-captain Hardik Singh scored twice each. Shilanand Lakra, Nilakanta and Jugraj Singh also got on the scoresheet.India chief coach Craig Fulton was pleased with Mandeep's performance."He (Mandeep) was good, he did full of running and was nice and sharp, which was important," he said.Despite the convincing result, Fulton felt India needed to perform better in the third quarter, after the teams changed ends."We wanted a fast start, which we got in the first quarter. We wanted to play some fast-flowing hockey, which we did. But the third quarter wasn't that good, and that remains a problem. But I am glad we finished strongly," he pointed out.India had to manage without midfielder Manpreet Singh, who has been ruled out of the tournament because of a calf muscle injury. Hardik, Vivek Sagar Prasad and Nilakanta took charge of the midfield against Bangladesh and combined well with the forwards.Mandeep was a major threat in attack, with Abhishek, Dilpreet, Shilanand and Sukhjeet Singh supporting him.At the back, Harmanpreet, Amit Rohidas, Jugraj and Sanjay will continue to shoulder responsibility, while Suraj Karkera and Krishan Bahadur Pathak are the goalkeeping options.India will face a less familiar opponent in China, who pushed Asian Games silver medallists Malaysia hard before going down 4-5 in their opening match.China have brought an entirely new squad for the tournament, with their young players showing promise against Malaysia. Their lack of recent exposure against India, however, makes them a difficult team to assess.Fulton admitted that India had limited information about their opponents."This Chinese team is unknown to us, as they have come here with a completely new group, not the one that played at the Asian Games. We don't know much about them and haven't seen them play. We will have to analyse video footage of their match to get a fair idea about them," Fulton said.India will aim to carry their attacking form into Thursday's match while addressing the concerns raised by their coach. China, meanwhile, will look to build on their close contest against Malaysia and challenge the defending champions.Malaysia will face South Korea, while Japan will take on Bangladesh in the other matches scheduled for Thursday.Goalkeepers: Suraj Karkera, Krishan Bahadur PathakDefenders: Sanjay, Harmanpreet Singh (captain), Amit Rohidas, Jugraj Singh, Jarmanpreet Singh, Amandeep LakraMidfielders: Rajinder Singh, Aditya Arjun Lalage, Nilakanta Sharma, Hardik Singh, Vivek Sagar PrasadForwards: Shilanand Lakra, Abhishek, Sukhjeet Singh, Dilpreet Singh, Mandeep Singh
Article Summary: India will face China in their second round-robin match on Thursday. The five- time champions began their title defence with a big win over Bangladesh. Harmanpreet Singh-led side scored eight field goals and five goals from set pieces against Bangladesh.

Article Title: Nagaland United to add a new chapter to Talimeren Ao’s legacy by becoming first club from Nagaland on national stage with IFL debut
Article Text:
NUSC Stadium (left) and Talimeren Ao

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On the 107th anniversary of independent India’s first captain, Talimeren Ao, on Jan 28 last year, a new football stadium was inaugurated at the foothills of the Naga Hills in Chümoukedima, and a one-year-old club from the municipality played its first competitive match.Nagaland United FC lost that game 2-3 to Barak FC but wrote a new chapter in the football fate of the state that had given India the skipper who led the country from the front barefoot at the 1948 Olympics in London, carrying with him a nascent nation’s hopes in its first international campaign.And, on a chilly evening in Srinagar on Friday, Nagaland United will continue that legacy, albeit after a gap of 78 years, when they take on hosts Real Kashmir in the Indian Football League opener at TRC Stadium and become the first club to represent the northeastern state on the national stage.“Our aim in our debut IFL season is to build a competitive, disciplined, and fearless team that represents Nagaland with pride,” coach Kaizad Ambapardiwalla told TOI. “We want to compete strongly in every match, establish our identity through attacking football, high intensity, and teamwork, and challenge ourselves against the best teams in the league.”This promotion of a two-year-old club into the second-tier competition was courtesy of another club from the region that stamped its authority at the top tier by winning the I-League in 2017 – Aizawl FC.Having won their first tournament in October last year with the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy title, the club from Chümoukedima got the chance to face Aizawl FC on June 6, who came calling to their neighbours under the banner of Football for Peace and a “Match for Peace, Goal for Hope”.The visitors won that game 2-0, but three months later, on September 9, the All India Football Federation approved a goodwill agreement for Nagaland United to take a cash-strapped Aizawl’s place in the IFL, as the Mizoram club pledged technical and development support.Taking on the baton from a former I-League champion that has represented northeast for eleven straight seasons in the national league without relegation, Nagaland United will look to add another chapter in the football history of Nagaland, but of the football-loving northeast.“For me, it’s more than just playing at a higher level: it’s an opportunity to give back to the club that gave me my start, represent my state with pride, and hopefully inspire the young players back home to believe that their dreams, too, are possible,” 19-year-old Nagaland United defender Thejangulie Zatsu told TOI.“I know my journey is far from over, and I just want to keep growing, give everything I have for this badge, and make everyone who has believed in me proud.”On the evening of October 30, across Nagaland, people will gather around the screens: in community halls, in living rooms, in shops with their shutters half down as Nagaland FC get the opportunity to add another chapter to the story that started a hundred years ago with a Naga boy chasing a pomelo across a mission playground in the Naga Hills.“As a defender myself, his journey means even more to me because I play in the same position (as Amo). It gives me something to look up to and reminds me that where we come from should never limit how far we can dream,” added Zatsu.Friday will see that dream continue its journey from the foot of the Naga Hills to the Himalayan valley in Kashmir.
Article Summary: Nagaland United FC will play in the Indian Football League for the first time in 78 years on Friday. The two-year-old club will take on hosts Real Kashmir at TRC Stadium in Srinagar. Nagaland will become the first club from the northeastern state to represent India on the national stage.

Article Title: ISL: An attacking contest on card as leaders NEUFC lock horns with Bengaluru FC
Article Text:

KOLKATA: Still unbeaten after three matches, despite the frustrating stalemate away in their last game, NorthEast United FC will be back on Friday to continue their winning run at home and stay at the top of the Indian Super League table.“The mentality. We go into every game with the mentality that we are no longer the underdogs,” head coach Juan Pedro Benali said at the pre-match interaction on Thursday.However, on the other half of the field at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati, will be a side that is also unbeaten in their ISL campaign and sit on the fourth spot having played one game less than the hosts.When NEUFC take on Bengaluru FC , it will be a test of the Highlanders’ defensive solidity – having conceded just one goal in three games – against the attacking prowess of the visitors, led by India striker Ryan Williams.NEUFC were held to a goalless draw by Odisha FC in their previous outing, with striker Alaaeddine Ajaraie missing a stoppage-time penalty, while Bengaluru registered a 2-0 win over Chennaiyin FC through goals from Williams and Mihailo Perovic.Benali believes that the challenge for NEUFC will be as much about breaking down Bengaluru’s structure as it will be about managing their attacking threats.“The details, concentration and crucial phases of the game will make the difference,” Benali added, underlining the fine margins that could decide the final scoreline.NorthEast United, meanwhile, will look to use their own attacking options and vary their approach to create openings. And, despite Ajaraie’s late penalty miss against Odisha FC in the last game, the Spanish coach kept his faith in the skills of their Moroccan talisman.“I prefer to win 4-3. I don’t want 0-0. I want to win. If there is a penalty tomorrow, Ajaraie will take it. There is no doubt about it,” Benali made it clear.Bengaluru coach Pep Munoz is also aware of the Ajaraie threat to their defence on the day.“They have an identity, some patterns that they like to create and a clear style of play,” Munoz said on Thursday, adding that his team is prepared to face either a back-four or a back-five defensive system.Going into the match after a break, Bengaluru will also hope to keep up their winning run as the fixture looks destined for an exciting contest of attack and defence for the fans.
Article Summary: NorthEast United FC take on Bengaluru FC in the Indian Super League on Friday. The Highlanders are unbeaten after three games and sit top of the table. Bengaluru are also unbeaten in their ISL campaign and sit in fourth place. NEUFC were held to a goalless draw by Odisha FC in their last game.

Article Title: 'Enjoying the game has to be the fundamental,' says Tvesa Malik after top-10 finish at India Open
Article Text:
Tvesa Malik (TOI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For Tvesa Malik, a strong performance at the Women’s Indian Open was as much about mastering her mind as it was about getting her golf right. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, carding a four-round total of one-under 287 (71, 73, 71, 72) to emerge as one of three Indians in the top 10. With Vani Kapoor finishing second and Pranavi Urs sharing fourth place, the home contingent enjoyed an encouraging week at the event.“I think everyone can see it. I’ve always been really proud of how, despite how small the Women’s Golf Association of India (WGAI) started out and how few girls have been playing, so many have gone on to play in Europe and overseas. It’s not an easy standard,” said Tvesa.The progress, she added, has been building for years, with Aditi Ashok establishing herself internationally before Pranavi Urs and other Indian golfers delivered strong performances, including at the Asian Games. The recent Women’s Indian Open, she felt, was another encouraging sign of that development.The emergence of young talent has also caught her attention. Ojaswini Saraswat, who made the cut at the Women’s Indian Open at just 13, offered a glimpse of the potential among the next generation. For Tvesa, however, the key to nurturing young golfers is ensuring that the desire to play comes from within.“A lot of the time, it’s actually their parents who come and ask questions about how they should proceed.For me, it has always been about enjoying the game. That has to be the fundamental. If that is there, the sky is the limit,” she said.She added, “Parents have an important role in helping young players pursue their ambitions, but the goals must ultimately belong to the children themselves.”While younger players today have access to better information and are developing their games at an early age, Tvesa believes they must also learn to manage expectations. The competition is becoming younger and more intense, making it important to balance ambition with patience.Reflecting on Ojaswini’s achievement, she said, “You have to realize that you’re still so young and there’s so much time. Continue learning, ride that experience, and, at the same time, don’t set expectations so high that they become unrealistic.”Tvesa’s own performance at DLF was a reminder of the importance of that balance. The demanding course, known for punishing inaccurate shots and misplaced approaches, requires players to remain composed even when things do not go according to plan.While her ball-striking had been encouraging, she felt her mental approach made the bigger difference during the week.“This year, I felt a bit more accepting of the course. When you play there and you’re from there, the expectations are always high. It’s such a fine line between pushing yourself and almost holding yourself back,” she said.Tvesa, who is familiar with the DLF layout, explained that a single mistake can have a significant impact because of the course’s demanding nature. Accuracy off the tee and precise approach shots are crucial, while missing a green in the wrong place can make even saving par difficult.Her ability to accept those setbacks and move on was particularly encouraging. She recalled how her caddie praised her composure after the final round.“My caddie said the biggest thing was not actually what I had played, but the fact that I didn’t get upset. That impressed him the most,” she said.For Tvesa, patience was the key. Rather than allowing a mistake to affect the rest of her round, she reminded herself that more opportunities would come.That mental adjustment is also central to the challenge she is working to overcome in her professional career. Although she feels her technique has improved significantly, the results have not always reflected the quality of her game.Tvesa, who is married to fellow professional golfer Ajeetesh Sandhu, said, “Your technique is good enough when you’ve practiced and played for this long. Then you have to find the small things that give you an edge. Awareness is a big thing, understanding where I’m making mistakes and why, rather than just spending all my time working on technique,”.Beyond individual performance, Tvesa believes Indian women’s golf needs stronger institutional support to sustain its progress. Drawing on her experience competing on the Ladies European Tour, she pointed to systems in countries such as Sweden, Germany, and Australia, where players receive assistance with accommodation, coaching, physiotherapy, and training facilities.“It’s an expensive game to play, and support is necessary for everybody. Having a team around a player also provides mental reassurance when travel, fatigue, and changing conditions affect performance,” she said.
Article Summary: Tvesa Malik was one of three Indians in the top 10 at the Women's Indian Open. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Vani Kapoor finished second and Pranavi Urs shared fourth place at the event.

Article Title: Mirabai Chanu pulls out of World Championships with back issue; Gyaneshwari Yadav finishes eighth
Article Text:
India's Mirabai Chanu (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Commonwealth Games silver medallist Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships on Thursday, while India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue.Gyaneshwari, 23, from Chhattisgarh, recorded a combined lift of 198kg, with 88kg in the snatch and 110kg in the clean and jerk, to finish on top of Group C. Her total was also better than those achieved by several lifters from Groups A and B.The Asian Championship silver medallist could have improved on her personal best of 199kg and secured a higher overall finish had she converted two missed attempts, one in each section.Chanu, meanwhile, was forced to pull out before making her much-anticipated debut in the 53kg category. She had been assigned to Group B with an entry total of 200kg but withdrew after experiencing back pain.China's Zhang Haiqin claimed the gold medal with a total of 221kg (98kg+123kg). American Eleanor Ulrey took silver with 220kg (98kg+122kg), while North Korea's So Hyon Kim secured bronze with 214kg (91kg+123kg).The snatch competition also saw seven lifters register lifts of at least 90kg, a benchmark Chanu has been working towards for more than six years.At the World Championships, lifters are divided into groups based on their declared entry totals, which represent the combined weight they intend to lift in the snatch and clean and jerk. Group A features those with the highest entry totals, followed by Groups B, C and D.The World Championships is among six events in the first phase of the qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Article Summary: Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships. India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue. China's Zhang Haiqin claimed the gold medal with a total of 221kg.

India will have a 17-member contingent, featuring 11 women and six men, competing across 11 sports at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal from October 31 to November 13.Table tennis player Syndrela Das, badminton talent Tanvi Patri and swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu are among the country's leading medal prospects at the fourth edition of the Summer Youth Olympics, which will be staged in Africa for the first time.Das will take part in the women's singles table tennis competition, while Asian Under-17 badminton champion Patri will represent India in the women's singles event. Desinghu is entered in three swimming events: the women's 100m freestyle, 200m freestyle and 200m individual medley.India's participation will span athletics, archery, badminton, beach wrestling, boxing, equestrian, judo, swimming, table tennis, windsurfing and wushu. The 17-athlete squad will be the country's smallest contingent at a Summer Youth Olympic Games.The 2026 edition will be held across Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly over 15 days. Around 2,700 athletes are expected to compete in 25 sports for 153 medal events. Ten additional engagement sports will also be part of the programme, but will not offer medals.Dakar 2026 will mark the first time an Olympic sporting event is held on African soil.The Games were initially scheduled for 2022 but were postponed by four years due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The previous Summer Youth Olympics took place in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 2018.India have collected 23 medals across the three previous editions, comprising three gold, 16 silver and four bronze. The inaugural Games were held in Singapore in 2010, followed by Nanjing in China in 2014 and Buenos Aires in 2018.Organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the Youth Olympic Games are designed for athletes primarily aged between 15 and 17. Alongside sporting competition, the event features educational and cultural programmes aimed at promoting Olympic values, participation and international understanding.The 2026 sports programme includes athletics, swimming, breaking, skateboarding, beach handball, beach wrestling, futsal, coastal rowing, Baseball5 and Wushu Taolu, among others. Baseball5 and Wushu Taolu will make their Youth Olympic Games debut. Ten engagement sports, including golf, karate and surfing, will be held without medal events.
Article Summary: India will have a 17-member contingent, featuring 11 women and six men, competing at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Table tennis player Syndrela Das, badminton talent Tanvi Patri and swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu are among the country's leading medal prospects. The 2026 edition will be held across Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly over 15 days. Around 2,700 athletes are expected to compete in 25 sports for 153 medal events.

Article Title: Warning bells despite series victory: Seifert, Phillips, Milne expose India's flaws in Hamilton

New Zealand's Tim Seifert, right, bats during the T20 cricket international between New Zealand and India in Hamilton, New Zealand, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026.

India may have pocketed the five-match T20I series 3-2, but Sunday's crushing seven-wicket defeat to New Zealand in Hamilton exposed several cracks that will concern the team management ahead of the ODI leg starting on Nov 4.For the second successive match, India's bowling lacked penetration and their fielding failed to back it up as New Zealand chased down 192 with ease at Seddon Park. Tim Seifert blasted a breathtaking 93 off 50 balls, while Glenn Phillips capped a dream series with an unbeaten 65 off 38 deliveries as the hosts romped home with 12 balls to spare.Earlier, Adam Milne's fiery spell of 4-19 had ensured India were restricted to 191-8 despite half-centuries from Ishan Kishan and captain Shreyas Iyer.The biggest talking point before the match was India's continued reluctance to hand teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi an opportunity despite the game being a dead rubber. Instead, Sanju Samson retained his place and endured another disappointing outing, falling for four. Apart from his 67 in the opening match, Samson failed to make an impact in the series and compounded a poor evening by dropping Phillips on 31.India's innings appeared set for a grandstand finish after Kishan and Iyer launched a counterattack following early setbacks. Abhishek Sharma fell for one while Samson's struggles continued, leaving India under pressure at 18-2.Kishan, returning after missing two matches because of a low-grade adductor strain, looked in sublime touch from the outset. The left-hander hammered 61 off just 32 balls, striking five fours and five sixes. At the other end, Iyer finally rediscovered his rhythm, racing to a 22-ball fifty, his fastest in T20Is. The pair added 93 runs in only 43 balls for the third wicket and powered India to 111-2 after 10 overs. A total in excess of 200 looked possible at that stage.However, New Zealand's bowlers staged an impressive comeback. Blair Tickner dismissed Kishan while Nathan Smith removed Iyer with a well-directed short ball. Milne's pace and bounce troubled the lower order and India managed only 80 runs in the second half of the innings. Naman Dhir's 33 and Nitish Kumar Reddy's 22 provided late impetus, but the visitors ultimately finished short of what would have been a par score.The chase belonged almost entirely to New Zealand. Seifert survived an early reprieve when Naman Dhir dropped him on 13 and made India pay dearly. He added 73 runs with Daryl Mitchell before combining with Phillips in an 86-run stand for the third wicket that effectively ended the contest.Phillips once again showcased why he is among the most destructive T20 batters in the world in the middle order. Fresh from his century in the previous match, he struck eight fours and three sixes and finished the series with a record-breaking 341 runs in five matches.There was one bright spot for India. Kishan's knock took his tally to 1,220 T20I runs in 2026, surpassing Suryakumar Yadav's record for the most runs by an Indian in a calendar year and helping him cross the 2,000-run milestone in T20Is.
Article Summary: New Zealand beat India by seven wickets to win the T20 series 3-2. Tim Seifert hit 93 off 50 balls as New Zealand chased down 192. Glenn Phillips capped a dream series with an unbeaten 65 off 38 deliveries. India's bowling lacked penetration and fielding failed to back it up.

Article Title: 180 runs, 1 wicket, 4 T20Is! 'Playing Bhuvneshwar Kumar was a mistake': Ex-India star questions selectors
Article Text:
Bhuvneshwar Kumar (BCCI Photo)

Bhuvneshwar struggles in New Zealand series

Pathan says young pacers missed an opportunity

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'The question is definitely about the timing'

NEW DELHI: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has questioned the selectors' decision to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar back into the T20I team, calling his inclusion in the recent series against New Zealand a mistake.Bhuvneshwar returned to India's T20I side after a gap of four years but struggled to make an impact. He managed just one wicket while conceding 180 runs in four matches.India, led by Shreyas Iyer, started the five-match series with three consecutive wins but lost the final two games. Following the series, Pathan questioned the purpose of bringing back the experienced pacer when the next T20 World Cup is still some distance away."In my opinion, where did the selectors go wrong? They made a mistake by playing Bhuvneshwar Kumar in this series. Look, there is no doubt that Bhuvneshwar is a good bowler and a senior player. However, playing him here, when the T20 World Cup is nowhere near, was questionable. If you were preparing Bhuvneshwar for the 50-over World Cup, which is closer, that would have made sense," Irfan said in a video on his YouTube channel.Bhuvneshwar's comeback in the first T20I did not go as planned. Playing his first T20I in four years, he went wicketless and conceded 49 runs in four overs at an economy rate of 12.25.He picked up his only wicket of the series in the second T20I, dismissing Daryl Mitchell for six. However, he conceded 50 runs in his four overs.The experienced pacer went wicketless again in the third match, giving away 40 runs. He missed the fourth T20I before returning for the series finale.Bhuvneshwar was unable to make an impact in the final match as well. He conceded 41 runs in four overs without taking a wicket.Pathan believes Bhuvneshwar's selection also meant that young fast bowlers missed out on valuable international experience."By including him in this series, however, you missed out on giving young fast bowlers an opportunity. A youngster could have played in his place and gained valuable experience. Mayank [Yadav] could have played all the matches and gained that exposure, while Prince Yadav could have played too. You missed a valuable opportunity for your fast bowlers to gain good experience on New Zealand soil," he added.Pathan also made it clear that his comments were not based only on Bhuvneshwar's performances in the series. He acknowledged that the senior pacer was also unlucky at times."I'm not saying this because Bhuvneshwar didn't perform well. That's not the case. Although he was a bit unlucky-he bowled well in his first two overs, but later, when he bowled the final over of the powerplay, he conceded runs. These things happen to any player. There is no question about his skill," he noted.Pathan said the selectors should focus on giving young fast bowlers opportunities, especially on pitches where they have little room for mistakes."The question is definitely about the timing. Would this have been a better opportunity for a young fast bowler? I believe it would have been. You have to understand that if you want to develop fast bowlers, it is very important to give them opportunities and let them play on true pitches, where the margin for error is very low," he explained.
Article Summary: Bhuvneshwar returned to India's T20I side after a gap of four years. He managed just one wicket while conceding 180 runs in four matches. Former India all- rounder Irfan Pathan has questioned the selectors' decision.

Article Title: 400 and counting: Why India are ahead of the curve in six-hitting
Article Text:
Abhishek Sharma has hit 86 sixes in this calendar year for India. (PTI)

Batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker. Julian Wood | Power-hitting coach

India's Abhishek Sharma, left, and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AP/PTI)

I think the quality of batting has improved significantly. Players have also started playing fearless cricket. They don't have the inhibitions that batters may have had earlier. Hariesh Jaikumar | Sunrisers Hyderabad batting coach

Everybody knows that Test cricket and ODI cricket complement each other, but T20 cricket is now a different beast. Julian Wood | Power-hitting coach

Poll Vote & Share your view Which factor do you think has contributed the most to India's success in T20 cricket? Power-hitting capability Team strategy and planning Player fitness and training 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: India hit 289 sixes in 40 T20Is in 2022. Four years later, they have smashed 400 in the same number of matches, a staggering 38.4 per cent increase. And the six-hitting spree is far from over. It has merely been put on hold for eight weeks, with Shreyas Iyer's men set to resume their big-hitting exploits against Sri Lanka in a three-match T20I series in December.On the second ball of the 19th over against New Zealand, Naman Dhir's top-edge sailed over fine leg and landed 15 rows back in the stands. It was India's 400th six in 2026, making them the first team to reach this monumental milestone. Of those, 142 have come against New Zealand, the most India have hit against any opposition in a calendar year.India's six-hitting prowess was also one of the reasons behind their 3-2 series win against New Zealand. Indian batters smashed 142 sixes, compared to New Zealand's 61. In pure numbers, that is a difference of 486 runs.A majority of India's six-hitting has come from the designated top three, with Abhishek Sharma leading the way with 86 sixes, followed by Ishan Kishan (60) and Sanju Samson (50). It also tells the story of why India are the only team to have crossed the 100-run mark in the Powerplay twice.India have smashed 145 sixes in the first six overs alone. Across their 40 matches, Indian batters have amassed 2,681 runs in 239 overs, at a blistering strike rate of 189.96 and a staggering run rate of 11.21.These numbers reflect India's dominance in T20I cricket, having won back-to-back T20 World Cup titles. Renowned power-hitting coach Julian Wood believes India's approach to batting is vastly different from that of other teams."I think India are approaching T20 cricket differently from other nations. They're batting differently and not managing risk in the traditional sense. Instead of managing risk, you have to master the skill, and I think Indian batters are doing that very well," Julian Wood, the power-hitting coach, tells TimesofIndia.com."India probably have the largest pool of players playing T20 cricket in the world, which means they're adapting to the evolution of the game quicker. The game has evolved massively and will continue to do so, but India are definitely ahead of the curve at the moment," he adds.While flatter pitches and smaller boundaries are often cited as reasons behind the surge in six-hitting, Wood believes the evolution of batting has left bowlers with very little margin for error."Batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker," he says.Citing Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's ability to hit all around the ground, from mid-off to fine leg, Wood explains that bowlers have little margin for error against such aggressive batters. "If you're going to bowl wide to him, you'd probably have to bowl wide and full. But you have to execute that delivery perfectly. The problem for bowlers is that when they miss, the ball doesn't just go for four; it goes for six. That puts them under tremendous pressure. "Wood points to Sooryavanshi's sixes off Jasprit Bumrah and Pat Cummins in the IPL as examples of this changing mindset. "It's almost as if there's a lack of respect, but he knows that if the bowler misses, he can hit him for six. The mindsets of both batters and bowlers have changed. Batters now think, 'If he misses, I'm going to hit him for six.'"I've worked a lot with Liam Livingstone. When he was at his peak, his mindset was similar. He knew that if the bowler executed his skill perfectly, he might get him out. But if the bowler missed, he would hit him for six. That kind of mindset is very dangerous."Sunrisers Hyderabad batting coach Hariesh Jaikumar echoes Wood's sentiments, attributing the evolution of T20 batting primarily to the improvement in batting standards."You have to give credit to the batters. People say the pitches have become flatter, but even three or four years ago, similar pitches were being prepared," he told this website."I think the quality of batting has improved significantly. Players have also started playing fearless cricket. They don't have the inhibitions that batters may have had earlier. The game itself has evolved completely," he adds.One of the biggest changes in Indian batting since the defeat to England during the 2022 T20 World Cup has been the emphasis on occupying the crease and the shift away from relying on finishers to provide the big hits towards the end. Today, it is the openers who are dominating the Powerplay."I think a new breed of cricketer is emerging. Players who were traditionally finishers are now batting higher up the order. Instead of asking them to face just 10 to 15 balls, teams want them to face more deliveries," explains Wood."When those players move up the order, the batters coming in behind them are also hitters with the mindset to attack from ball one. That's how I see the game evolving. In five years, teams could be full of this type of cricketer. The top eight batters could all be players who just want to smash the ball. We're already beginning to see that," he says.Wood believes the evolution of T20 cricket has also had a positive impact on the 50-over format and Test cricket, particularly by encouraging batters to adopt a more aggressive approach."The game is phenomenal. T20 cricket will help 50-over cricket, as we've already seen. Sri Lanka, for instance, chased 430 against India and England. It's great for the game. Everybody knows that Test cricket and ODI cricket complement each other, but T20 cricket is now a different beast," he says.India's 400 sixes are more than just a statistical milestone. They reflect a shift in batting philosophy, where power-hitting is no longer the preserve of finishers but a skill expected across the top order. As Wood points out, the next phase of T20 cricket could see teams packed with batters who attack from ball one. India, meanwhile, are already giving a glimpse of what that future looks like.
Article Summary: India hit 289 sixes in 40 T20Is in 2022. Four years later, they have smashed 400 in the same number of matches. Abhishek Sharma leads the way with 86 sixes, followed by Ishan Kishan and Sanju Samson. India are the only team to have crossed the 100-run mark in the Powerplay twice.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

India returned from the Asian Para Games in Nagoya with its best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, powered by world records, golden doubles and medal-winning debuts. TOI picks out the ones who stole the show. .. MONA AGARWAL : A golden double and a world recordMona Agarwal won the women’s 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold before setting a world record in the 50m rifle three positions SH1. Her score of 357.5 secured a second title and made her the first Indian para-shooter to medal in the event. The Jaipur-based Paris Paralympics bronze medallist trained for the 50m event with a rented rifle, travelling long distances to train. PRANAV SOORMA : Two titles, two recordsPranav Soorma claimed the men’s discus throw F51/52/53 gold with an Asian-record effort of 11.66m, then added the club throw F51 title with a Games-record 32.87m. Paralysed after a spinal cord injury at 16, Soorma rebuilt his life through education and sport. His Nagoya double followed club throw gold at the previous Asian Para Games and silver at the Paris Paralympics. NISHAD KUMAR : Two disciplines, two gold medalsNishad Kumar ventured beyond his high jump speciality to win the men’s T47 long jump with an effort of 7.11m, then claimed high jump gold with a Games-record clearance of 2.04m.The double Paralympic silver medallist took on the additional discipline despite a troublesome knee, showcasing his versatility.SIMRAN SHARMA: Silver to goldSimran Sharma won the women’s 200m and 100m T12 titles, improving on her two silvers at the previous Games. The visually impaired sprinter from Ghaziabad followed her 200m triumph with a Games-record 12.02s in the 100m, finishing ahead of Iran’s Hajar Safarzadeh.SHEETAL DEVI: Golden comebackSheetal beat Singapore’s Nur Syahidah Alim in the women’s individual compound final. She also won women’s compound doubles silver with Payal Nag and mixed-team gold.FINAL BOWMona Agarwal with the Indian flag at the closing ceremony on Saturday.

Third Paralympics, one big dream: Gold at LA 2028

IAS officer by day, shuttler by night

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. She also extended her congratulations to the entire Indian contingent.Para athletics was India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze.India also won 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery and five in para shooting. The contingent added two medals each in para judo and para powerlifting.The closing ceremony brought together athletes, officials and dignitaries to mark the conclusion of the Games. Asian Paralympic Committee president Majid Rashed declared the event closed, highlighting the growing strength of para sport across Asia and its role in building a more inclusive society.Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also praised the athletes' determination, teamwork and sportsmanship, describing their performances as a reminder of the “profound beauty” of para sports.The Asian Para Games began in Guangzhou, China, in 2010, evolving from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled. The Aichi-Nagoya edition was the fifth staging of the event, with Doha, Qatar, scheduled to host the sixth in 2030.For India, the closing ceremony marked the end of a historic campaign — one that raised the country's medal benchmark and showcased the depth and growing strength of its para-sport movement.

A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.

NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, after a record-breaking final-day flourish in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.India collected nine gold medals on the day — their biggest single-day haul of the ongoing edition — with champions emerging from badminton, archery, shooting and athletics. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.Athletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.

Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep at the Asian Para Games. Pranav Soorma defends his title in the men's club throw F51 event. Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar complete all-Indian podium finish.

Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan

Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.

Guardiola's life after leaving Manchester City

A Beautiful Obsession
