Pep Guardiola's life has changed considerably since he left Manchester City after a decade in charge, but reports linking him to a luxury property in Barcelona date back to before his departure. The mansion, reportedly worth £13.5 million, is in the exclusive Pedralbes district, close to the former family home he once shared with Cristina Serra. Recent reports have now brought the property back into focus, although neither the purchase nor its ownership has been confirmed.



The Sun first reported in November 2025 that Guardiola was considering a newly built luxury mansion in Pedralbes, one of Barcelona's wealthiest and most private neighbourhoods. The property was valued at approximately £13.5 million and reportedly offered sea views, a private swimming pool, gym facilities and a jacuzziThe development was marketed as a collection of exceptionally private homes, with promotional material describing the villas as “super-luxe”. Its brochure stated: “The space, light and views are more powerful than anything that can be built.”It added: “The scope of each super-luxe villa stretches far beyond its four walls and expansive grounds. The only limit is the horizon – as far as the eye can see.”The development's landscaping was also designed to provide residents with privacy, featuring evergreen oaks, lemon trees, cypresses, magnolias and ancient olive trees.Much of the attention surrounding Guardiola's reported interest, however, centred on the property's location. The mansion was said to be less than 100 yards, or approximately 90 metres, from the £8.5 million Pedralbes residence he previously shared with his estranged wife.Guardiola's relationship with Brazilian journalist and fashion entrepreneur Cristina Serra has attracted considerable attention since reports of their separation emerged. The couple, who had been together for around three decades, reportedly began divorce proceedings in 2024.Several Spanish outlets, including reports cited by The Sun, suggested that tensions developed after Guardiola extended his Manchester City contract until 2027 without fully discussing the decision with Serra. She had already returned to Barcelona several years earlier, while Guardiola continued living primarily in Manchester.According to Spanish broadcaster Antena 3, Serra eventually moved out of the family's long-time Pedralbes residence and relocated to a private flat in Barcelona's Eixample district.The situation was more complicated than the suggestion that Guardiola was purchasing a property immediately beside his estranged wife's home. Reports indicated that the former marital estate was being preserved as a family investment and a potential future residence for their youngest daughter, Valentina. The couple have three children together.There were also suggestions during 2025 that the separation might not be permanent. In April that year, Spanish media personality Maria Lapiedra told EN Blau that the pair were attempting to reconcile.“Pep Guardiola and Cristina Serra still wear their wedding rings. They're trying to reconcile,” she said.“He came to her house for three days this Easter and stayed the night there.”Lapiedra also claimed that Guardiola had suggested travelling regularly between Manchester and Barcelona to spend time with Serra. Those comments offered a different picture from reports that the couple had completely moved on from their relationship.Guardiola's reported Barcelona property plans have taken on greater significance since he left Manchester City in the summer of 2026, bringing an end to a ten-year managerial spell that produced 18 major trophies, including six Premier League titles and the club's first Champions League triumph.Rather than immediately taking another managerial position, the 55-year-old stepped away from the daily demands of coaching. He retained a connection with the City Football Group through an ambassadorial and technical advisory role, allowing him to contribute to projects across its network without returning to the dugout.Guardiola has also spoken about wanting to experience life outside football after spending much of his adult life immersed in the sport. In an interview featured in the Amazon Prime documentary, he reflected on the pressures of his final years at City and his decision to prioritise his family, including his 95-year-old father.“Right now, I honestly don't feel any desire to return to management. I am trying to discover life outside of football. For ten years, my mind was running at one thousand miles per hour every single day. Now, I just want to be a son to my 95-year-old father, a present father to my children, and simply see what else the world has to offer when you aren't worrying about the next match,” he said.His immediate plans have consequently centred on taking a break rather than finding another club. He has previously expressed an interest in managing a national team, but his longer-term intentions remain open, with no confirmed timetable for a return to coaching.Recent reports have also suggested that Guardiola is already living in Barcelona, with the Pedralbes mansion again being linked to his name. However, there has been no confirmation that he has completed the reported £13.5 million purchase, leaving the precise ownership and living arrangements unclear.
Article Summary: Pep Guardiola is reportedly eyeing up a £13.5m mansion in Barcelona. The property is located less than 100 yards from the home he shared with Cristina Serra. The couple have three children together. Guardiola left Manchester City in the summer of 2026.

Five yellow cards would normally leave Lionel Messi facing a one-match suspension in any other league, but the Inter Miami captain will be available for Sunday's meeting with New England Revolution. His reprieve comes through one of Major League Soccer's less familiar regulations, which allows players to have cautions removed from their disciplinary record after a sustained run of good behaviour.Messi picked up his fifth yellow card of the 2026 MLS season during Inter Miami’s 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday, October 28. The booking came in the 44th minute, after the Argentine approached referee Armando Villarreal following a collision involving Cincinnati defender Samuel Gidi. Under MLS’s regular-season disciplinary rules, five yellow cards ordinarily bring a $250 fine and an automatic one-match suspension, which would have ruled Messi out of Sunday's meeting with New England Revolution.However, the league's Good Behaviour Incentive allows a player to remove one caution from his accumulated total for every five consecutive appearances without receiving a yellow card, red card or supplemental disciplinary sanction.Messi has completed two such qualifying runs this season, reducing his active tally from five bookings to three and keeping him available for Inter Miami's next match.The provision appears in the league's official Competition Guidelines:“A player will automatically reduce his yellow card accumulation total by one yellow card each time he appears in five consecutive matches without receiving a yellow card, red card or supplemental discipline in such matches.“For clarity, a player cannot have a negative yellow card accumulation total; the Good Behavior Incentive can only reset to a zero-card total. This incentive will be automatically applied a maximum of three times throughout the course of the MLS Regular Season.”The reduction takes effect once the fifth qualifying match has been completed. A player can benefit from it a maximum of three times during the regular season, although the accumulation cannot fall below zero.Messi's disciplinary record during the 2026 MLS regular season shows how the incentive has kept him below the suspension threshold. He has received five bookings, but two separate runs of five consecutive matches without disciplinary action reduced his accumulated total by one caution each time.His bookings and the subsequent reductions unfolded as follows:The two reductions explain why Messi's latest booking did not take him to the five-card suspension threshold. Although he has been cautioned five times during the campaign, his official accumulation stands at three.Messi's reprieve comes ahead of Inter Miami's meeting with New England Revolution on Sunday, with the two sides separated by just two points. The result could have a significant bearing on the Eastern Conference standings, as a victory for Kily Gonzalez's side would take Inter Miami above its opponents and into second place with one game remaining.The clubs last met on April 26, 2026, when they played out a 1-1 draw at Inter Miami's home ground. Carles Gil and Germán Berterame scored in that encounter, leaving Sunday's fixture with an opportunity for either side to gain an advantage in the closing stages of the regular season.A higher finish would also bring better seeding for the MLS Cup, a competition Messi will be hoping to lead Inter Miami to win for the second time. The Argentine has been central to the club's campaign, scoring 25 goals in 29 appearances and leading the league's scoring charts as he pursues the Golden Boot.Had the Good Behaviour Incentive not reduced his accumulation, Messi's fifth booking against Cincinnati would have left him facing a suspension. Instead, he is available for a fixture that could determine where Inter Miami finishes in the Eastern Conference.

Mohun Bagan SG coach Panos Dilmperis and green-and-maroon faithful in the stands must have gone through a remarkable rollercoaster of emotions as the team crossed the Punjab FC hurdle with a hard-earned, come-from-behind 2-1 win in their Indian Super League match at Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday.The hosts fell behind to Alfred Planas' third-minute goal before Lee Erwin fired home the equalizer in 18 minutes. Mohun Bagan then needed a slice of luck to go ahead in the 42nd minute when Dejan Drazic's shot took a wicked deflection off Punjab FC defender Bijoy V and settled into the net, proving to be the match winner.The Southern Derby had all the ingredients of a gripping contest but a goal as Chennaiyin FC and Kerala Blasters FC played out a goalless draw at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Chennai in the early ISL match of the day.

KOLKATA: Armed with hard-won lessons from last season, East Bengal women are on a mission to scale a new continental summit for Indian football. The two-time IWL winners begin their group stage campaign in the AFC Women's Champions League against Vietnamese Ho Chi Minh City WFC here on Sunday.In the last year's campaign held in China's Wuhan, Anthony Andrews ' Moshal Girls became the first Indian side to win a match in the group stage of Asia's premier women's club competition but agonizingly stopped short of progressing to the quarterfinals after losing their last match 0-3 to PFC Nasaf of Uzbekistan. Had East Bengal lost that match 0-2, they would have progressed to the knockout stage.Now drawn in Group B, Anthony Andrews' Moshal Girls will also take on South Korea's Hwacheon KSPO WFC on Nov 4 and North Korea's 4.25 SC three days later. In a first for Indian football, East Bengal have been given the honour of hosting the AWCL Group Stage matches and their all three matches at Kishore Bharati Krirangan will kick off at 8pm."Last season's heartbreak helped us understand much better in terms of what the players should do at the bigger level. Obviously the game is faster at the international level and that's how we have strengthened the side this season.We have played a few good tactical games to understand if we can solve problems what we had faced last season," Andrews told reporters during the pre-match news conference at a New Town hotel on Saturday."The girls are ready to put their best foot forward," added the 30-year-old, who is also working with India's U-17 women's team as an assistant coach.The top two from three groups of four teams as well as the two best third-placed sides will advance to the quarterfinals from the 12-team group stage.With a mission to accomplish in Asian football, the red-and-gold management has bolstered the side with the acquisition of India internationals Rimpa Haldar and Thoibisana Chanu as well as Japan's Hitomi Tanaka and Ghanaian trio Olivia Anokye, Adama Alhassan and Abigail Antwi.East Bengal have qualified for the group stage for the second consecutive season after topping Group A in the competition's preliminary stage in Malaysia last Aug in breathtaking style, scoring 18 goals in three games and conceding none.Home is where the team's hopes lie now and midfielder Sathi Debnath is determined to make the most of it."The Kishore Bharati Krirangan has been a bastion of the club and this is the venue where I had got my first trophy with East Bengal women's team (Kanyashree Cup in 2023)," the midfielder said."Because of some momentary lapses, we missed out on the quarterfinal berth by a whisker last season. Article Title: Why Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, refuses to drink milk: Inside the diet and discipline behind his longevity, according to former chef
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo's former chef reveals why the 41-year-old superstar refuses milk as part of his strict diet and fitness routine.

Why Ronaldo refuses to drink milk

What Ronaldo eats throughout the day

Ronaldo maintains under 10% body fat, avoids refined sugar, milk, and focuses on strict recovery routines/ Instagram

The training and recovery behind his longevity

Ronaldo’s recovery routine includes intense sauna sessions and ice baths to maintain peak fitness and longevity/Instagram

Why Ronaldo's former chef agrees with Haaland about organ meat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At 41, Cristiano Ronaldo is still chasing a milestone that once seemed beyond the reach of any footballer, with his career tally approaching 1,000 goals after another prolific season for Al-Nassr. His longevity has been built on an unusually disciplined approach to training, recovery and nutrition, although one of the strictest rules in his diet concerns a food that many athletes regard as an everyday source of protein and calcium. According to his former private chef, Giorgio Barone, Ronaldo does not drink milk at all.Milk is commonly included in athletes’ diets because of its protein, calcium and other nutrients, with many players using it as part of their recovery routine. Ronaldo, however, has avoided dairy as part of his long-standing nutritional approach, a decision his former private chef says reflects more than a preference about taste or performance.Giorgio Barone, who previously worked as Ronaldo’s private chef, explained that milk was completely excluded from the forward’s diet because of his views on humans consuming the milk of other animals.“No milk,” Barone told Covers.com, before explaining his reasoning.“Humans are the only animals that drink the milk of other animals. No other animal drinks milk after three months. Calves don’t drink milk after the age of three months. Animals don’t drink the milk of other animals.“It does not exist in nature. Only human beings continue to drink milk up to 30, 40, 50, and 60 years, and in my view it is wrong. We breastfeed from our mothers, like dogs, wolves, cows and donkeys. It is normal.“After infancy it is not normal. It is against nature.”Barone's explanation is his own view of nutrition, rather than an established medical consensus, but it illustrates how deliberately Ronaldo has approached the food he consumes throughout his career. Dairy is not the only category he avoids, with the Portuguese forward also known for steering clear of refined sugar, processed foods and alcohol.Barone described Ronaldo's diet as balanced rather than built around a single food group, with the emphasis placed on fresh ingredients, lean protein and vegetables. The former chef said the forward eats a little of everything, provided it meets the standards of his nutritional routine.“Cristiano Ronaldo’s diet is balanced,” he said. “He eats a little bit of everything, but it’s always healthy.”Breakfast typically includes avocado, coffee and eggs, with no added sugar. Lunch can consist of chicken or fish accompanied by vegetables, while dinner is generally lighter, with fish or meat served alongside vegetables.“Starting with breakfast, he would have an avocado with coffee, eggs and no sugar. Absolutely no sugar. Lunch could be chicken, fish and always vegetables. If he needs carbohydrates, he gets them through vegetables, so he doesn’t need anything made with flour.“Nothing like pasta, bread and other types of food. In the evening, he eats light foods, usually fish or meat in the form of fillet. It’s always accompanied by vegetables.”The broader nutritional approach described in the additional account of Ronaldo's routine includes as many as six high-protein meals a day, spaced three to four hours apart. Chicken, cod, sea bass, fresh vegetables and avocado feature prominently, while quinoa and other whole grains provide carbohydrate sources alongside the vegetables mentioned by Barone. The emphasis remains on whole foods and consistent meals rather than relying on processed products or sugary snacks.That routine is designed to support the physical demands of a player who continues to compete at the highest level well into his forties. Ronaldo's body fat has been reported at below 10 per cent, with some accounts putting it at around seven per cent, although the exact figure can vary with the timing and method of measurement.Ronaldo's approach extends well beyond what he eats. His training combines high-intensity sprinting, plyometric exercises and explosive strength work with Pilates and other forms of conditioning, while recovery has remained an important part of his daily routine.His recovery methods include sauna sessions, ice baths and cryotherapy, with his partner Georgina Rodriguez also known to join him for some of those activities.Sleep is another area in which Ronaldo has reportedly adopted an unconventional approach. Rather than relying solely on one long overnight period, he utilizes polyphasic sleep to optimize his recovery. His routine consists of five 90-minute naps spaced throughout the day, a strategy meticulously designed to maintain high metabolic energy levels and maximize cellular repair between intense training sessions.The combination of nutrition, training and recovery has helped Ronaldo remain physically competitive across a career spanning more than two decades. His longevity has also made him unusually conscious of the small decisions that can affect his preparation, from the food he eats to the time he gives his body to recover between matches.One of the most visible examples of his attitude towards nutrition came during the 2021 European Championship. At a press conference, Ronaldo moved bottles of Coca-Cola away from the table and encouraged viewers to “drink water”. The gesture attracted enormous attention and was followed by a reported fall in Coca-Cola's market value.Barone also discussed the differences between Ronaldo's nutritional choices and those of Manchester City striker Erling Haaland, who has spoken about including raw milk in his diet. The two approaches differ on dairy, but Barone agreed with Haaland's preference for organ meats, which he considers particularly nutritious.“I agree with [Erling Haaland’s diet of] eating the organs. The liver, heart and brain are all healthy foods. They are superfoods. Cristiano liked liver too. I love it. It’s very rich in iron, and it’s important in the diet, so for the organs, I approve, but not for the milk.”Ronaldo's customized routine has continued to attract global attention because of what he manages to sustain on the pitch. The 41-year-old forward has elevated his historic, all-time record tally to 985 official career goals following a masterful performance for Al-Nassr. His latest Saudi Pro League appearance against Al-Kholood featured a dazzling 15-minute hat-trick that secured a thrilling 5-3 victory. This incredible treble marked the 67th senior career hat-trick for the Portuguese icon, extending his unparalleled scoring record even further ahead of long-time rival Lionel Messi.The performance came shortly after Ronaldo was named the winner of the inaugural B.O.A.T. award, or Ballon d'Or of All Time, following a global fan poll that selected his 2008 season with Manchester United as the greatest peak campaign. With the updated career total placing him 15 goals short of 1,000, the milestone is now a realistic target as he continues to lead Al-Nassr and Portugal.His pursuit of that record has brought renewed attention to the discipline behind his career, including the strict nutritional choices described by Barone. For Ronaldo, avoiding milk is one part of a much larger routine built around consistency, preparation and the demands of remaining an elite footballer at 41.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's former chef reveals why the 41-year-old superstar refuses milk as part of his strict diet and fitness routine. Giorgio Barone says Ronaldo does not drink milk because humans are the only animals that drink the milk of other animals. Ronaldo's recovery routine includes intense sauna sessions and ice baths to maintain peak fitness and longevity.

Article Title: The exact points that separated Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe in Ballon d'Or race revealed as official voting figures emerge
Article Text:
Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe by just 28 points to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or, official voting figures reveal.

Kane edges Mbappe after a closely fought vote

London, Oct 27 (IANS) England captain Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or in a ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre.

Where Kane's victory ranks among the closest Ballon d'Or decisions

Kylian Mbappe backs Ballon d'Or hopes after historic World Cup campaign

Putellas wins the women's award, but the lower places are exceptionally tight

Harry Kane's first Ballon d'Or came after a much tighter contest than the final announcement might have suggested. Kylian Mbappe finished just 28 points behind the Bayern Munich striker, with the official voting figures now revealing how the 100-member jury divided its support between the two leading contenders.Kane finished with 1,055 points from the 100 journalists who voted for the men's Ballon d'Or, just 28 ahead of Kylian Mbappe, who received 1,027. The narrow gap shows just how close the race was between the two stars.Kane was named the winner on 40 of the 100 voting ballots, while Mbappe received the top spot on 23. Those votes helped the England captain secure the award, although Mbappe remained firmly in contention until the final results were counted.Kane lifted the trophy at the London Palladium on Monday evening, becoming the first Englishman to win the men's Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001. He earned the honour after scoring 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England during the 2025-26 season, helping Bayern win a domestic Treble and captaining England to third place at the World Cup.For Mbappe, it was another near miss in his first attempt to win the award. Kane's 28-point lead was also smaller than the 41-point gap between Rodri and Vinicius Junior in 2024, making this one of the closest Ballon d'Or races in recent years.Although Kane and Mbappe were separated by only 28 points, their contest was not the closest in the award's history. The figures released by L'Equipe place it among the more closely contested recent editions, but several previous winners have prevailed by even smaller margins.Lionel Messi defeated Virgil van Dijk by seven points in 2019, making it the narrowest margin of recent voting contests. The result followed a season in which Van Dijk had helped Liverpool win the Champions League, while Messi collected his sixth Ballon d'Or.The historical margins become even tighter when earlier editions are considered. Matthias Sammer beat Brazilian forward Ronaldo by a single point in 1996, while Sir Bobby Charlton also finished one point ahead of Eusebio in 1966. Only 22 people voted in that 1966 edition, a considerably smaller electorate than the international panel used today.The comparison is useful because the Ballon d'Or's voting structure has changed considerably over the decades. Kane's 28-point victory came from a system in which 100 journalists each selected 10 players, giving every ballot considerably more scope to influence the final standings than the smaller electorate of earlier editions.The official breakdown covers the top 10 in both the men's and women's awards. The men's panel consisted of 100 journalists, while 50 journalists voted for the Ballon d'Or Feminin, making 150 voters across the two categories.Under the system introduced in 2022, the men's award is voted on by journalists representing the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings, while the women's award uses representatives from the top 50. Only one journalist from each eligible country is entitled to submit a ballot.Each voter selects 10 players from the respective list of 30 nominees. The players are then awarded points according to their position on each ballot: 15 for first place, 12 for second, 10 for third, followed by eight, seven, five, four, three, two and one point.That structure means the maximum possible score is 1,500 points for the men's award and 750 for the women's. Kane's 1,055 points represented more than two-thirds of the maximum available, while Mbappe's 1,027 left him only 28 behind.The awards considered performances during the 2025-26 season. That distinction also applied to players whose circumstances changed after the campaign: Rodri, who now plays for Barcelona, was assessed on his performances for Manchester City and his World Cup success with Spain.The men's top 10 showed a substantial gap between the leading pair and the rest of the field. Barcelona's Lamine Yamal finished third with 881 points, 146 behind Mbappe and 174 short of Kane. Rodri was fourth with 726, followed by Lionel Messi on 612.The women's Ballon d'Or produced a more comfortable victory at the top, although the voting figures also revealed several close contests further down the standings. Alexia Putellas won the award for a third time, equalling the record held by her Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati.Putellas, who now plays for London City Lionesses after representing Barcelona during the 2025-26 season, received 618 points. Her former Barcelona team-mate Ewa Pajor finished second with 532, leaving an 86-point gap between them. Putellas' total was also more than four-fifths of the maximum 750 points available in the women's vote.The battle for third place was particularly close. Manchester City forward Bunny Shaw collected 334 points, just two more than Lyon's Melchie Dumornay, who finished on 332.There was also little to separate the players further down the rankings. Patri Guijarro finished fifth with 221 points, while Caroline Graham Hansen and Pernille Harder both collected 220. As the two players were tied on points, their final positions were decided by the number of first-place votes, with Graham Hansen placed sixth and Harder seventh.Claudia Pina and Arsenal's Alessia Russo also finished level on 155 points. Their final positions were decided using the same tiebreaking rule, while Temwa Chawinga completed the top 10 with 113 points.
Article Summary: England captain Harry Kane has won the 2026 Ballon d'Or in a ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre. Kane finished with 1,055 points from the 100 journalists who voted, just 28 ahead of Kylian Mbappe, who received 1,027. Alexia Putellas won the women's award, but the lower places are exceptionally tight.
